terms.gloss: a society, a club: a circle of members who meet
evidence: Cic. Sen. 45: sodālitātēs autem mē quaestōre cōnstitūtae sunt
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a society, an association of any kind, especially for religious purposes; also a dining club. Its members are sodālēs (see member). The senate once dissolved the political clubs (Cic. Q. Fr. 2.3.5, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an association of people with one calling: a guild, a college
terms.comment: A body of colleagues bound by common rules: priests, magistrates, merchants, craftsmen.
Classically a circle of people gathered to talk (see group); Morgan–Owens uses it for a club.

phrases.latin: Sodālitātēs autem mē quaestōre cōnstitūtae sunt sacrīs Īdaeīs Magnae Mātris acceptīs. Epulābar igitur cum sodālibus omnīnō modicē.
phrases.english: Clubs were founded when I was quaestor, when the Idaean rites of the Great Mother were taken up. So I used to dine with my fellow members, quite moderately.

sources: Lewis & Short: sodalitas · Lewis & Short: collegium · Lewis & Short: circulus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: organization, society, association; organization: club.
